Air Pollution Prediction Commons

About

The goal of the appc package is to provide daily, high resolution, near real-time, model-based ambient air pollution exposure assessments. This is achieved by training a generalized random forest on several geomarkers to predict daily average EPA AQS concentrations from 2017 until the near-present (currently June 2026) at exact locations across the contiguous United States (see the model-performance report for more details).

APPC collects and harmonizes EPA AQS outcomes and handles model development, evaluation, and prediction. The geomarker package supplies the environmental predictors.

Model generation 3 uses geomarker 0.2.0, with coverage from January 1, 2017 through June 30, 2026. It was trained on 618,918 daily observations at 786 EPA AQS locations. Daily leave-one-location-out cross-validation gives a median absolute error of 1.20 micrograms per cubic meter and median Spearman correlation of 0.84. See the model-performance report for the full evaluation, including interval coverage.

The trained model, training dataset, checksums, and provenance are paired in the model generation 3 release. predict_pm25() downloads and verifies the model on first use; the model/data release must be published for that download to be available. The v2 release and evaluation cover the same dates. Aggregate cross-validation performance is similar, with slightly different observations from refreshed EPA data.

Installing

Install the latest stable release of appc from R-universe with:

install.packages("appc", repos = c("https://geomarker-io.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

Install the latest, under-development version of appc from GitHub with:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("geomarker-io/appc")

Example

In R, create model-based predictions of ambient air pollution concentrations at exact locations on specific dates using the predict_pm25() function:

appc::predict_pm25(
  x = s2::as_s2_cell(c("8841b39a7c46e25f", "8841a45555555555")),
  dates = list(as.Date(c("2025-05-18", "2025-06-10")), as.Date(c("2025-06-22", "2025-09-20")))
)

See more examples in the timeline example.

You can also pass a geomarker s2cd object directly. Its stored dates are used:

locations <- geomarker::s2cd(
  s2::as_s2_cell(c("8841b39a7c46e25f", "8841a45555555555")),
  dates = list(as.Date(c("2025-05-18", "2025-06-10")), as.Date("2025-06-22"))
)
appc::predict_pm25(locations, keep_predictors = TRUE)

Environmental predictors

APPC uses the geomarker package for environmental predictor assessment. See its documentation for S2 location/date inputs, available geomarkers, and source-data management.

Data storage

Environmental downloads and assessment are managed by geomarker under its own R user data directory. See geomarker’s data and offline-operation documentation for cache and source-refresh options. APPC retains AQS outcomes, assembled training data, and fitted models under tools::R_user_dir("appc", "data"). Set R_USER_DATA_DIR to choose a different root for both packages.

Developing

The committed workflow has two steps:

just make_training_data
just train_model

The first script downloads and harmonizes AQS outcomes, calls the shared geomarker-backed predictor assembler, prints coverage/missingness summaries, and saves training_data_v3.rds. The second reads that table and fits the existing GRF specification, saving rf_pm_v3.rds. These are large, manually invoked jobs. Neither is run by package checks.

Use terra 1.9.46 or newer to avoid the compressed NetCDF extraction slowdown in earlier 1.9 versions. The training-data script normally refreshes current-year AQS outcomes. After a successful AQS refresh, you can reuse that annual cache when restarting predictor assembly:

options(appc.refresh_aqs = FALSE)
source("inst/make_training_data.R")

Training requires geomarker 0.2.0 from release commit 373820d0ab8082f856f7bf0f639f3128111d825a. Install the exact dependency recorded in DESCRIPTION from the repository root:

pak::pak(".")

The minimum runtime dependency is geomarker 0.2.0. The exact version, release tag, source SHA, feature settings, and coverage are recorded in inst/model-v3-spec.dcf. Training checks the installed version and source SHA; a development version number alone does not identify the code. Artifacts preserve this specification, session information, and geomarker’s source manifests. Retain the assembled training artifact to reproduce fitting after upstream AQS or weather revisions. Use a dedicated R_USER_DATA_DIR for an official build so existing local monthly MERRA overrides are not picked up unintentionally. No automatic NASA source refresh is performed.

Existing artifact files are protected against overwriting. Move an existing v3 artifact aside before rebuilding. V3 models require metadata and predictor names matching the model specification. The distributed model is verified against its registered release checksum.

Run just render_model_dash to evaluate the model. Set APPC_BUILD_MODEL_ARTICLES=true when rebuilding model-dependent pkgdown articles. Ordinary package checks skip these large jobs. The existing v2 performance report remains available with the v2 release.
